brief: Goldman's Prime Brokerage weekly rundown (Oct 2) reports the S&P 500 down 0.3% on the week despite a Friday rally, as investors digested a weak NFP print, an in-line ISM Manufacturing survey, and a demanding macro backdrop (oil, rates, geopolitics). Softer PCE and NFP data eased rate expectations (30bp of cuts now priced through year-end), triggering short covering in Russell 2000 futures: open interest fell $900mm since 9/29 and RTY funding spreads richened, though the desk says sustained RTY outperformance needs durable rate relief before end-user length rebuilds. US Fundamental long/short net leverage fell a third straight week to 46.4% (2nd percentile, five-year), with equities modestly net bought on short covering in Macro Products that offset continued Single Stock shorting; Health Care was the most net-bought sector via short covering while Energy was net sold for a sixth straight week despite oil near multi-year highs. NDX hit a new all-time high even as the equal-weight S&P fell for a seventh straight week, reflecting mega-cap concentration; the desk likes IWM and QQQ upside into Q3 earnings and the midterms, arguing the market is underpositioned for EPS, especially in tech.
